parts:
Redirecting to -dev.

On Wed, 2013-11-27 at 20:57 -0500, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> I don't think there is a problem here; in fact as.array for stanfit
> calls extract but with parameters other than the default. It is just
> the results returned in different forms that take different amount of
> time.
>
>
> I do not know how or even if something like stanfit[i, j, k] can be
> implemented in R.
The help for Methods has an example of overriding the [] operator:
setMethod("[",
signature(x = "myFrame"),
function (x, i, j, ..., drop = TRUE)
{
S3Part(x) <- callNextMethod()
x@timestamps <- c(Sys.time(), as.POSIXct(x@timestamps))
x
}
)

I'm not sure if anything needs to go in the namespace to support this.

It looks as if the sim$samples[[ic]][[n]] in a stanfit object gives a
vector whose k'th element is the k'th step of chain ic for parameter n.

I guess the default extract is slower because the permutation requires
more work.

I'm not sure if accessing elements through 2 lists is noticeably slower
than accessing array elements.

Ross

messages.author: edd4914c326b6d31
messages.subject: Re: rstan: extract vs as.array timing [patch 20x speedup]
parts:
[Redirected to -dev]

Profiling the code showed that it was spending most of the time in the
unlist method called by sapply in the first line of
fun1 <- function(par) {
sss <- sapply(tidx[[par]], get_kept_samples2, object@sim)
if (is.list(sss)) sss <- do.call(c, sss)
dim(sss) <- c(sum(n_kept), object@sim$dims_oi[[par]])
dimnames(sss) <- list(iterations = NULL)
sss
}
that is part of the extract method for stanfit. This function is
called only if permute is true.

Why that's so slow I don't know. Using lapply instead of sapply runs
fast for that line, but triggers the do.call(c, sss) on the next line,
which is about as slow as the original. However,
fun1 <- function(par) {
sss <- lapply(tidx[[par]], rstan:::get_kept_samples2, object@sim)
if (is.list(sss)) sss <- do.call(cbind, sss)
dim(sss) <- c(sum(n_kept), object@sim$dims_oi[[par]])
dimnames(sss) <- list(iterations = NULL)
sss
}

Runs much faster (since I defined the test function outside of the
package scope I needed to explicitly qualify calls to internal package
functions).

e1 is the original extract; e2 is the new version.
> system.time(t1 <- e1(myfit))
user system elapsed
11.420 0.004 11.463
> system.time(t2 <- e2(myfit))
user system elapsed
0.396 0.008 0.405
!> identical(t1, t2)
[1] TRUE


I think the lines
if (is.list(sss)) sss <- do.call(cbind, sss)
dim(sss) <- c(sum(n_kept), object@sim$dims_oi[[par]])
could be converted to
do.call(cbind, sss)
but perhaps I'm missing some subtlety. As I said, they look as if they
might be a holdover from an earlier implementation.

Ross

On Tue, 2013-12-03 at 14:01 -0800, Ross Boylan wrote:
> Profiling the code showed that it was spending most of the time in the
> unlist method called by sapply in the first line of
> fun1 <- function(par) {
> sss <- sapply(tidx[[par]], get_kept_samples2,
> object@sim)
> if (is.list(sss)) sss <- do.call(c, sss)
> dim(sss) <- c(sum(n_kept), object@sim$dims_oi[[par]])
> dimnames(sss) <- list(iterations = NULL)
> sss
> }
> that is part of the extract method for stanfit. This function is
> called only if permute is true.

The sense in which unlist is called by sapply may not be obvious (it
wasn't to me)--it has nothing to do with the get_kept_samples2 function.
Rather, sapply is
> sapply
function (X, FUN, ..., simplify = TRUE, USE.NAMES = TRUE)
{
FUN <- match.fun(FUN)
answer <- lapply(X = X, FUN = FUN, ...)
if (USE.NAMES && is.character(X) && is.null(names(answer)))
names(answer) <- X
if (!identical(simplify, FALSE) && length(answer))
simplify2array(answer, higher = (simplify == "array"))
else answer
}
and simplify2array ultimately calls unlist.

Here's a sample call stack from Rprof:
"unlist" "as.vector" "simplify2array" "sapply" "FUN" "lapply" ".local" "extract" "standardGeneric" "extract"
(outermost call on the right, apparently, and "FUN" is the function fun1 in the source).

If anyone is curious, here is the profile of the original function:

> e <- extract(myfit)
> Rprof(NULL)

On Tue, 2013-12-03 at 19:17 -0500, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> Thanks. I think it might not be good to do that for
> * it need do the boundary check, which makes it inefficient
> * the thinning makes the index for iteration ambiguous

More generally, it's unclear exactly what interface would be of general
interest. I originally was thinking

stanfit[i, j, k] where i is chain, j is step and k
is coefficient.

As you point out, one might want j to be before or after thinning.
k could be an index (in the total index sense used internally), a string
like the values of pars, or booleans. The total index seems an
unfriendly interface, though perhaps if some of the related functions
were exposed it would make sense.

One might want to overlook the chains and use
stanfit[n, k] where n is the n'th sample (combining all chains), and k
indexes a parameter.

It might need some caching (e.g., of the total indices for a named
parameter) to be effficient. I'm not sure it needs bounds checking; I
think it will just throw an error if one attempts an out of bounds
access.

There are also several choices about what gets returned.

All of which is to agree that the time is not ripe for implementing [].
Now that extract is faster I feel less need to work around it.

Ross

Adding back the deleted dim-setting line seems to work:
             fun1 <- function(par) {
               sss <- lapply(tidx[[par]], get_kept_samples2, object@sim)
               sss <- do.call(cbind, sss)
               # essential for 2 dimensional parameters
               dim(sss) <- c(sum(n_kept), object@sim$dims_oi[[par]])
               dimnames(sss) <- list(iterations = NULL)
               sss
             }

BTW, on a quick test the code is a bit over 10x faster than the current production code for 2-dimensional coefficients.
